scope: Sourced feature analysis for the AI assistant chat slice; proposal only

ux.reason: AIScreen describes Chat and Agent modes, composer, history and proposal cards, but the mobile route renders UnbuiltPlace; route realization is part of the feature seam.

screens.reason: The package screen defines message list, composer, privacy/history controls, context banner, artifact and proposal dialogs; the actual mounted route is currently a placeholder.

state.reason: The screen and hook maintain chat/agent tab, privacy mode, stream status, active run, history, proposal, attachments and thread state; the relation between UI and persistence is not proven.

errors.reason: The provider converts request failure to fallback stream text and a failed event; thread, quota and mission calls often return null or empty on failure, so visible errors and retry behavior need a contract.

feedback.reason: The screen wires haptic feedback for send, selection, errors and success, plus busy/stream states and tool-call cards; end-to-end event behavior is unverified.

motion.reason: Navigation, dialogs, drawer and streaming have transitions, but no sourced motion specification; the future role handoff needs motion, reduced-motion and cancellation requirements.

accessibility.reason: Controls and message list have labels, but this source pass does not establish screen-reader behavior, focus movement, keyboard coverage or reduced-motion compliance.

data.reason: The hook composes role, class, gap, memory and domain context; PJC declares reflection exclusion, but actual sanitization and privacy behavior need scoped evidence.

api.reason: The hook uses /api/ai/chat and /api/ai/threads while SanctuaryCloudProvider targets /api/v1/ai/chat; the inspected API catalog does not establish an admitted AI capability.

database.reason: AiMessage models thread, user, privacy mode and expiry, but runtime writes, expiry enforcement, ownership and sync paths were not demonstrated.

dependencies.reason: The AI package declares TanStack AI dependencies and the lockfile resolves them; upstream compatibility/latest status was not researched and remains unknown.

security.reason: The hook sends an auth token and BYOK key in request context and composes class/memory context; PJC names review and reflection-exclusion requirements, but no complete security/data-flow proof was inspected.

offline.reason: The flow specifies an offline fallback and the provider emits a local-storage reassurance on errors, but draft persistence and offline recovery were not confirmed.

reuse.reason: AIScreen composes owned native UI components; platform rules require corresponding owned web/native contracts and prohibit ad hoc production UI.

reuse: Reuse the owned native UI components already used by AIScreen; if web is in scope, use the owned web component contracts.
Preserve the existing route; it currently renders UnbuiltPlace and must not be described as a working chat screen.
Resolve the API capability and channel against the API catalog and /api/v1 contract before wiring a new procedure.
openQuestions: Which requester decision admits an AI capability in the Sanctuary API catalog, and what resolves the observed /api/ai versus /api/v1/ai path mismatch?
Does Incognito mean no persistence at client, local database, sync and remote layers? PJC labels this user-origin, but implementation evidence and policy admission are absent.
What are saved and temporary retention, expiry, deletion, export and thread ownership rules? AiMessage has privacy_mode and expires_at, but enforcement was not inspected.
What context is allowed for each actor and entry? PJC excludes private reflections while the hook composes memories, gaps, role and domain envelope; an allowlist and tests are needed.
Is the requested slice text chat only, or does it include attachments, citations, tool calls, artifacts, history and autonomous missions? PJC is broader than the brief.
How should unauthenticated, expired-token, quota, timeout, malformed stream, offline and partial-stream states recover without losing drafts or implying success?
Which web and native route/screen are in the first admitted slice? FlowDAG lists /ai, the mobile route is a placeholder, and AIScreen is a separate package component.
What tests prove route reachability, stream behavior, access isolation, retention/expiry and offline recovery? No such test evidence was inspected in this bounded pass.
Which dependency versions and compatibility matrix are approved? Manifest and lockfile establish declared/resolved versions only; upstream status is unknown.
